subject: Energy
title: Helium-3 and Lunar Mining
description: Learn Helium-3 and Lunar Mining in one minute.

hook.text: The Moon's surface contains helium-3—a rare isotope that could fuel clean fusion reactors with no radioactive waste.

buildup.text: Solar wind has deposited helium-3 in lunar soil for billions of years—Earth's magnetic field blocks it from reaching us.

discovery.text: Helium-3 fusion produces only charged particles—no neutrons, meaning no radioactive reactor components.

twist.text: We haven't achieved helium-3 fusion yet—it requires even higher temperatures than deuterium-tritium fusion.

climax.text: China's Chang'e program is studying lunar helium-3 deposits—long-term energy could drive the next space race.

punchline.text: Mine the Moon for fuel—a sci-fi dream that physics allows.
